<aside class="blog-tldr not-prose"><div class="blog-tldr__label">TL;DR</div><div class="blog-tldr__body">
- Reconciliation hits five procedures
- Quality and cost both score
- Track choice changes upside caps
- CFOs need episode-level visibility
</div></aside>

For hospital CFOs, CMS TEAM changes the shape of **Medicare reimbursement.** Hospitals still bill fee-for-service, but at reconciliation — six months after each performance year — CMS compares actual episode spending to a risk-adjusted target price and issues a bonus or claws back a repayment.

## How do CMS TEAM target prices work?

Target prices are built from three years of regional baseline data, trended forward, with a discount factor (1.5–2%, per the finalized episode-specific discounts), a normalization factor, and beneficiary/hospital risk adjustment. A high-cost outlier cap at the 99th percentile protects against catastrophic episodes.

## How much revenue is really at stake?

According to Rainfall Health, up to **20% of Medicare revenue** is at stake for mandated hospitals and the company estimates up to **$85 million** in upside over five years — proprietary company figures, not independently verified. Independent estimates are more measured. Optum Advisory reports that "56% of mandatory participants are projected to lose money under current criteria unless they meaningfully improve performance," with losses averaging $1.2 million per facility. Brandeis University and the Institute for Accountable Care anticipate up to two-thirds of participants losing revenue on net; the American College of Surgeons, citing that analysis, notes AJMC modeling in which "the 62% of hospitals with estimated losses would lose an average of $1,350 per episode, whereas the 38% of hospitals with estimated gains would earn approximately $900 per episode."

On unit economics: the average readmission in a TEAM episode "costs roughly $14,000," per Milliman, and TEAM hospitals had average 2024 30-day LEJR episode costs of $18,723, per Trilliant Health.

## What is the stop-gain/stop-loss math?

Track 3 caps gains and losses at 20% of the target amount. On $5 million in annual TEAM payments, maximum risk or bonus would be roughly $1 million.

## No downside in 2026 — but 2027 is coming

There is no mandatory downside risk in Performance Year 1 (2026). Downside begins in 2027. CFOs should use 2026 to model exposure by episode and by operating physician.

## Frequently asked questions

### When does downside risk begin under CMS TEAM?

Downside financial risk begins in Performance Year 2, which is calendar year 2027.

### How are CMS TEAM target prices set?

Target prices are built from three years of regional baseline spending, trended forward, and adjusted with a discount factor, a normalization factor, and beneficiary/hospital risk adjustment.

### What is CMS TEAM's episode discount factor?

The discount factor is 1.5–2%, depending on the episode category.

### How much can a hospital lose under CMS TEAM?

Under Track 3, gains and losses are capped at 20% of the target amount for the episode.

### What does Rainfall Health estimate is at stake financially?

Rainfall Health estimates up to 20% of Medicare revenue is at stake for mandated hospitals, and up to $85 million in five-year upside for a system that performs well — company-stated figures, not independently verified.

### What do independent analysts say about CMS TEAM financial risk?

Optum Advisory projects 56% of mandatory participants will lose money absent performance improvement, averaging $1.2 million per facility; Brandeis University and the Institute for Accountable Care put the share of hospitals losing revenue on net as high as two-thirds.
